correctness.rationale: The discrete Sobolev inequality supplies Hilbert-space reproduction and \(\ell^{p_*}\) boundedness. The positive Green function has exactly \(2d\) maximal noncentral coordinates. Orthogonal decomposition of a near-maximizer reduces the normalized \(q\)-th power to \(b^q(1+A_q)+R_q\); the Hölder estimate \(|R_q|\le Cqt(\rho_d+t)^{q-p_*}\) and two concentration improvements yield \(t=O(\rho_d^qe^{C\sqrt q})\). Therefore \(R_q=o(\rho_d^q)\), \(b^q=1+o(\rho_d^q)\), and \(A_q=2d\rho_d^q+o(\rho_d^q)\) proves the precise limit for both scalar fields and all integer \(d\ge3\). No finite calculation is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete original and published initiating paper gives only the exact \(\ell^\infty\) Green point-evaluation constant and a nonsharp finite-\(q\) bound. The exponential correction and its first-shell coefficient are not stated nor directly implied without new quantitative near-extremizer control. Public research and web comparisons did not reveal a stronger covering statement for the same energy, lattice geometry and limiting regime; abstract perturbation coverage remains a disclosed risk.
residual_risks: A general abstract perturbation theorem for reproducing-kernel Hilbert embeddings might yield the same first-shell asymptotic as a corollary without matching title or terminology.
Finite-graph and nonlinear graph papers could not all be examined in full; their available mathematical objects differ materially from the stated quadratic infinite-lattice theorem.
No claim of independence, peer review, exhaustive literature coverage, or external certification is made.

value.rationale: The optimal \(\ell^q\) embedding norm is a natural quantitative invariant of the standard homogeneous lattice Dirichlet form. Its leading gap from the known \(\ell^\infty\) endpoint has the exact geometrical decay base \(\rho_d\) and shell multiplicity \(2d\). The theorem covers every integer \(d\ge3\), is not an arbitrary finite slice, and supplies information absent from the published endpoint constant.
